item.title: Tiger Woods ‘Still Fully Believes’ He Can ‘Beat Anyone’ at Golf Despite ‘Dealing With So Much Pain’
item.description: ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Tiger Woods wants to be a champion — and anything less is going to be very hard for him to accept as he prepares to return to the world of professional golf at the Hero World Challenge tournament in the Bahamas in December, a source tells Globe . “Even with everything that’s happened, Tiger still fully believes he can, and will, beat anyone on the course,” reveals the source. “It’s a great mindset, but it’s also worrying because a lot of people think he’s setting the bar too high.” Over the years, Woods, 50, has sustained several injuries, per AP , including a ruptured Achilles tendon and ACL, and undergone multiple back surgeries. As Globe previously reported, the 82-time PGA Tour champion also recently completed a stint in rehab in Switzerland after rolling over his Land Rover in Jupiter, Florida, on March 27. He was charged with a DUI but pleaded no contest to a lesser charge that will see his driver’s license suspended for five years. “His body just isn’t what it used to be,” admits the source. “He’s still dealing with so much pain. Everyone is telling him that just making this comeback is incredible, regardless of whether he wins or not, but Tiger doesn’t want to hear that.” Instagram/Tiger Woods Girlfriend Vanessa Trump is “very supportive, but she also doesn’t want to see him overdo it or get down on himself if things don’t go his way,” says Globe ‘s source. At the same time, “she’s also got to protect her own peace,” the source adds. In late October, Donald Trump Jr. ‘s ex-wife, 48, announced on Instagram that she is officially cancer-free after undergoing treatment for cancer earlier this year. “She’s been through so much with her health,” notes the source. “She needs her life to be as stress-free as possible and that is going to be hard if Tiger’s putting all this pressure on himself.” Read More From Globe Professor Who Claims His Affair With a Student Was Like 'Fatal Attraction' Accused of Sexual Assault Man Named Captain America Accused of Murdering Coworker, Demanding Money From His Girlfriend Kentucky Teacher Charged With 30 New Counts of Abuse, Human Trafficking of Minors After Prior Arrests This story Tiger Woods ‘Still Fully Believes’ He Can ‘Beat Anyone’ at Golf Despite ‘Dealing With So Much Pain’ first appeared on Globe . item.title: GB's Davis Cup-winning captain ends 17-year stint
item.description: Leon Smith guided Great Britain to their first Davis Cup title in 79 years [Getty Images] Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith is stepping down after almost 17 years in the role. Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936. The 50-year-old Scot will leave his role after next week's Finals in Bologna, where he is hoping to create "another special memory" by leading the team to the title once again. Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible. Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 victory, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time. "It has been an enormous privilege to lead the team for so many years, and I feel now is the right time, both for me personally and for the team moving forwards," Smith said. "Winning the Davis Cup in 2015 will always be one of the proudest moments of my career, but there are countless other experiences and memories that I'll cherish forever." With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign. Murray was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career. "He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said. "I've obviously known Leon a long time, I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments. "I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain." item.title: Puka Nacua faces NFL ‘banishment’ under suspension guidelines
item.description: Before Week 11 of the 2026-27 NFL season kicked off, the league announced that one of its biggest stars, Puka Nacua , has been suspended for three games for violating the personal conduct policy . The timing of the suspension turned out to be beneficial to the Rams and Nacua. Nacua is currently on injured reserve, so he was set to miss the next three games regardless of his status with the league. The All-Pro pass catcher will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, December 14 . However, Nacua’s suspension does come with a strong warning from the league. NFL Insider Tom Pelissero shared further details about what any future violation or “failure to satisfy conditions of the diversion program” could entail. According to Pelissero, if Nacua does not comply with the diversion program or finds himself in trouble down the road, it “could lead to additional discipline, up to and including banishment .” MORE: Stephen A. Smith still holding out hope for Rams’ Super Bowl run Puka Nacua Suspension Must Be Wake-up Call Oct 18, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) warms up before the game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) At just 25 years old, Nacua has a long career ahead of him if he can stay healthy and out of trouble. The good news is Nacua voluntarily entered a holistic care and recovery facility in Malibu as his off-field issues began to pile up. “I feel like I’ve learned is it’s OK to ask for support,” Nacua said after his first stint in the rehab facility. “Little did I know that even just writing in a journal, as simple as that, and finding ways to express some of the things I have near and dear to my heart … it’s been a great improvement in my life.” With such a bright future ahead of him, let’s hope that Nacua continues to improve off the field and reflect on some of the mistakes he made. item.title: Does Villanova Basketball Have A Backcourt Problem?
item.description: Villanova has played just five games and there have been some strong reactions to the overall performance. Is it too early to make judgments and overreact? The answer is no. When a team rebuilds a roster that cost plenty of money, results are expected right away. Let’s not forget, in five games, Villanova has played two real opponents and have lost both games. With Michigan and Kansas coming up, it could get uglier if the team does not clean up. The main issue that needs to get cleaned up is in the backcourt. The point guard position has not been good enough. Elijah Crawford has made some plays early this season, particularly against Notre Dame in the opener, but it is becoming clear that he has not been good enough. Is it quick to say that he is not good enough to play in the Big East? That is yet to be seen, but the early returns have not been positive. Crawford was a big-time recruit coming out of high school before going to BYU and then UIC. He is not going to be asked to score much for Villanova. He is averaging six assists through five games with 2.2 turnovers. It is important that the team has a ball handler to set the offense up with what should be an improved frontcourt and Tyler Perkins on the perimeter. Darryl Simmons was also added this offseason. He has been a strong shooter from deep during his career. This is a valuable skillset off the bench. Simmons is already dealing with an injury that kept him sidelined against Pitt. We’re not going to mention how both Acaden Lewis and Bryce Lindsay are off to strong starts for their respective teams this season. We’re not going to do it. But if we were to, how different would it look? There is some time before Big East play begins. That is what really matters for Villanova. But to compete this year, the backcourt must get figured out.

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur vs. Ipswich Town Premier League Preview
item.description: It was a shockingly positive October for Tottenham Hotspur with a draw at Old Trafford and three wins to follow, including the amazing result at Stamford Bridge. Of course, that naturally led to a depressingly flat performance against Leeds right before the break, which sent Spurs back to the bottom half of the table, though thankfully out of the relegation zone as has been the case for much of the past two seasons. Back in action, Tottenham gets three matches against teams below it in the table before a home North London Derby the first weekend of December. This run begins with a visit from Ipswich Town, who sits joint-13th with 11 points through 10 contests; all three of its wins this season came in the first six matchweeks, with just two points taken across the most recent four fixtures. Spurs disappointed against Leeds, but really must be taking all three points on Saturday. With back-to-back wins at home for the first time in ages, the Lane should be fully behind this squad against an overmatched opponent. Roberto De Zerbi’s group must take things one match at a time, but the next three matches feel like a quite important stretch. Match Details Date : Saturday, November 21 Time : 10:00 am ET, 3:00 pm UK Location : Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London TV : USA Network (US) Prior to Ipswich’s brief return to the Championship, these two sides split the contests in 2024/25, with the road team claiming each victory. In North London, the Tractor Boys scored twice in the first half, and a Rodrigo Bentancur consolation was not enough to prevent Ipswich from earning its first win. The reverse fixture saw four Spurs goals at Portman Road: a Brennan Johnson first-half brace, plus tallies from Djed Spence and Dejan Kulusevski to firmly put it away. Optimistically on the rise The rise in the table, the stringing together of wins, and the conquest over Chelsea all point to the tangible ways this team is making progress, and much of this felt overdue after Spurs kept putting together pieces of strong performances without being able to fully earn the result. The underlying metrics still see the club as squarely mid-table, but the trend is absolutely in the right direction. On top of this, optimism rises with the squad list. James Maddison, Savio, and Lucas Bergvall are among those who are coming back and should make a substantial impact in the lineup. With Kulusevski and Mohammed Kudus already available, De Zerbi will have far more attacking options now at his disposal, even with Mathys Tel and Xavi Simons out. This combination of form and personnel should have Tottenham’s confidence growing every week. Contrast that with the visitors who are winless in four and have only taken points from teams who are currently in the bottom eight spots of the table. Call me foolish, but this sets up well for Spurs, as the home side should be able to break down an opposing defense that has allowed the second-most goals this season. item.title: #PostPulpit mailbag: What’s wrong with the Patriots defense?
item.description: Behind back-to-back blowout losses and losing Drake Maye to injury , the New England Patriots season has quickly derailed over the last two weeks. Now, they have plenty questions to answers after a much needed bye week. So, let’s get into some of those in this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. What has gone so wrong with the defense? They’re relatively healthy and have a lot of the same personnel as last year. Kuhr did a great job last year and really earned the official promotion to DC. So what happened? Along the same lines, do you think Gonzo is really the type of player who, now that he’s gotten his payday, is going to sit on his laurels for the remainder of his career? – TDDsDad Is the defense’s biggest problem the square peg or round hole – scheme doesn’t fit players or players don’t fit scheme – spyponder90 The Patriots defense has a litany of problems right now. Here’s how we’d break them down: Zone coverage: Statistically, the Patriots are the worst zone coverage team in football, ranking dead last in both EPA and passer rating allowed in zone coverage. Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was a step ahead of opposing offenses earlier this season with his disguises in the secondary, but teams have caught on while New England’s defensive backs have failed to live up to their potential. Some of the issues in zone coverage also tie back to the pass rush. The Patriots rank 20th in the league in four-man pressure rate, giving opposing quarterbacks time to find the voids in coverage. To generate pressure, New England has had to blitz, which then leaves more space for the offense to attack with at least one defender taken out of coverage — as seen on Jahmyr Gibbs’ 50-yard reception last week. Man coverage: The logical follow-up would be to play more man coverage, especially with New England’s talented cover corners. The Patriots already rank near the top of the league in man coverage rate, but no team can rely on man coverage for the majority of a game for several reasons. Without an effective changeup, opposing offenses have game-planned for man coverage and exploit it with beaters such as stacks and bunch formations. On top of that, the talented cover corners have again not been playing to their potential. Effort/tackling: New England is not a poor tackling team by the numbers, but the defense often doesn’t appear to be rallying to the football — a concern when Mike Vrabel has made effort and finish his No. 1 non-negotiable . Opponents are piling up yards after the catch and yards after contact against New England. That reached a new low last week, when the Lions generated 220 yards after the catch and another 135 yards after contact on the ground. The effort doesn’t always show up on film, either. item.title: Shannon Sharpe thinks he knows ‘the main reason’ why LeBron James left the Lakers
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images LeBron James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2026 after eight years with the franchise. The 41-year-old joined the Philadelphia 76ers in the off-season, and he seems to be having a great time there. The Lakers are doing well without him too. Since his summer move, there have been several theories about why James decided to leave the Lakers. Shannon Sharpe has now had his say on what he thinks happened. Shannon Sharpe says LeBron James left the Lakers because he was disrespected James has been one of the biggest names in the NBA for a long time, and when he joined the Los Angeles Lakers, many expected them to dominate. However, the Lakers won just one NBA Championship with The King in his eight years there, which is one of the reasons why things turned a bit sour in the end. Some fans wanted James gone because they believed that Luka Doncic was their real star and would take them to the next level on his own. Sharpe believes that was one of the reasons why James felt disrespected and decided to leave. He said on the Nightcap show : “I think the main reason LeBron left the Lakers is that he felt like they didn’t respect him anymore. “He felt like, ‘Look, I understand Luka’s better, but y’all just blatantly disregarded what I’ve done for you guys the last eight years. Do y’all not remember what transpired the last couple of years Kobe was here? “‘Because Kobe was hurt a lot, and do you remember when Kobe retired, that 60-point game? What y’all did in ’16 and ’17. Do y’all remember that? And then for you to have this kind of laissez-faire attitude, it’s just like, you know what, y’all don’t really appreciate it.’ “And he heard it: ‘We don’t need LeBron. We don’t want LeBron. We got Luka.'” LeBron James’ summer departure has worked out for everyone There was a big debate in the summer following James’ departure from Los Angeles. Some were of the opinion that the Lakers would struggle this season, while others believed that The King’s new team, the Philadelphia 76ers, would have problems because of him. However, when you look at the records of the two teams, they are pretty similar. Of course, the debate about James and the Lakers will go on until the end of the season and perhaps even beyond that point. However, we think people should just accept that his departure was the best move for all parties involved and move on. item.title: Ben Shelton completes feat only Rafael Nadal can match this century after latest win at the ATP Finals
item.description: Ben Shelton broke new ground in his career by reaching the semifinals of the ATP Finals for the first time. After Arthur Fils lost the first set of his third and final group stage match against Alexander Zverev on Thursday, Shelton ‘s spot in the final four was confirmed. The 24-year-old American had beaten Rafael Jodar in straight sets earlier in the day to boost his chances of advancing at the prestigious year-end tournament. Photo by Pascal von Büren/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images Ben Shelton matches Rafael Nadal after advancing at the ATP Finals With his triumph, Shelton became the youngest American since Andy Roddick in 2004 to reach the semifinals of the ATP Finals. He also became the first left-hander other than Rafael Nadal to do so this century. Nadal made the semifinals six times and advanced to the championship match twice: in 2010 and 2013. The legendary Spaniard never managed to win the title, however, despite making 11 appearances. Shelton qualified for the ATP Finals for the first time last year, but was knocked out in the round-robin stage. He went winless in his debut campaign, winning just one set throughout the run against Felix Auger-Aliassime. This time around, Shelton has tallied a record of 2-1 in the group stage, having beaten Fils and Jodar but losing to Zverev. The loss to the German was his seventh straight in their head-to-head and first since the US Open final. Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images Ben Shelton’s semifinal opponent at the ATP Finals in Turin After finishing second in the John McEnroe group, Shelton will face the winner of the Ivan Lendl group, Carlos Alcaraz, on Monday. Alcaraz secured his spot atop his group after beating Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe, both in straight sets. Shelton has faced Alcaraz five times on the ATP Tour and has only come out on top against him once. Shelton’s sole victory in the head-to-head came in the quarterfinals of this year’s US Open, where he emerged victorious in a five-set thriller. Alcaraz has since earned revenge by beating Shelton in the Paris Masters final to extend his lead in the rivalry to 4-1. Their upcoming clash at the ATP Finals will be their third on an indoor hard court.

item.title: 5 questions with the enemy ahead of Steelers-Eagles
item.description: Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers are looking to rebound this week as they head on the road to take on the 2-7 Eagles. We talked with Brandon Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation to figure out what’s gone wrong with Philadelphia’s season, and what we can expect for this game. 1. This Eagles roster is hardly recognizable from the squad that won the Super Bowl just two seasons ago. I think most fans are aware of the Jalen Hurts situation. Outside of that, can you summarize for Steelers fans what has gone wrong for the 2-7 Eagles this season? Brandon Gowton : For starters, I’d recommend checking out Jimmy Kempski’s “ Eagles season from hell ” tracker. The TL;DR version is that the Eagles have been really bad and injured. The new-look offense is even worse than it was last year … and it can’t just be blamed on injuries. The Eagles also looked bad on offense when they were healthy (see: the team scoring seven points in a Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears). The Eagles’ defense was supposed to be the strength of the team, but Vic Fangio’s unit has largely underwhelmed. Howie Roseman didn’t have a great offseason. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) | NCAA Photos via Getty Images This weekend’s schedule for Nebraska wrestling doesn’t grab the national headlines, but it will be a very important weekend for this team. After splitting a pair of duals against Top-10 opponents to start the year, the Huskers will take on #21 Penn Saturday at the Palestra in Philadelphia at Noon on ESPN+. The Quakers have a solid squad with seven ranked wrestlers — including at their first six weight classes. They’ll supply a stiff test for the Huskers who are coming off that 27-6 loss to #2 Oklahoma State last Friday. Up Next ➡️ Philly pic.twitter.com/pzTETtyXBy — Nebraska Wrestling (@HuskerWrestling) November 16, 2026 Nebraska will then compete at the Keystone Classic on Sunday in the same arena, so we could see some of these matches against Penn multiple times. Also at the Keystone Classic will be #6 Virginia Tech, #10 Missouri, #33 Rutgers and #40 Drexel. Unfortunately, the Hokies will not be sending a full squad — their lethal lineup of lightweights are all competing Tuesday at the All-Star Classic — so guys like #1 Bo Bassett at 141 pounds, #3 Aaron Seidel at 133, and #4 Caleb Henson at 149 will not be in the field. Also on Saturday, Nebraska is sending a squad of 12 wrestlers to compete at the Younes Hospitality Open, hosted by Nebraska-Kearney. Let’s get into our weight-by-weight preview of who some of the Husker wrestlers may see this weekend. Weight-By-Weight Preview 125 pounds Nebraska’s #5 Vincent Robinson is coming off the first loss of his Husker career, so I think we will learn a lot about the offseason addition based on how he bounces back against some tough competition. Against Penn, Robinson will face #25 Max Gallagher who is 1-0 on the year. Gallagher is solid, but I don’t think he’ll threaten Robinson much. The real test comes Sunday at the Keystone Classic where Robinson will be in a field that includes #28 Anthony Knox. Don’t let the ranking fool you — he’s an incredibly talented freshman. Knox won Super 32 three times in high school while also winning four New Jersey state titles and four matches at Who’s Number One. item.title: Orioles news: The O’s inquired about Hunter Goodman
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 26: Hunter Goodman #15 of the Colorado Rockies celebrates hitting a home run during the third inning against the Chicago White Sox at Rate Field on September 26, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Camden Chatters. We’re less than two weeks away from the expected MLB lockout that will almost certainly put baseball in a deep freeze for months. So far there haven’t been many marquee free agent signings, but a few teams have been active in retooling their roster before they’re indefinitely blocked from making transactions. The Orioles have not been one of them. The Orioles, according to multiple national baseball writers, apparently intend to be busy this offseason. Of course, what they intend to do and what they actually end up doing are two very different things. If the O’s actually are planning on making big changes, I would’ve hoped they would have already started. And yet! We’ve heard rumors linking the Birds linked to several different players, but nothing has materialized, and maybe it never will. The most recent name to come up as a possible O’s target is Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman, a two-time All-Star. The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal writes that the Orioles “were among the clubs to check in on Goodman early in the offseason,” but “the talks failed to advance, and no names were exchanged.” So, uh, that’s probably the end of that, barring one of the teams having a change of heart. It’s understandable that the Orioles were intrigued by Goodman, who led all catchers with 41 home runs this season (technically he hit nine of them as a DH, but let’s not pick nits). The O’s are in dire need of a catching upgrade over Carlos Narváez, preferably someone who can take more than half of the workload behind the plate so that Samuel Basallo can spend more time DHing than catching. Rosenthal notes that Goodman had offseason surgery on his non-throwing shoulder but is expected to be ready by spring training, which almost certainly won’t start in February anyway. The Birds would certainly be shooting high for Goodman, who is one of the best offensive catchers in the game and has three years of team control remaining. Over the last two seasons, Goodman has a .262/.317/.525 line with 72 homers and 179 RBIs. He’s not considered a very good defender, but with a power bat like that, you don’t need to be. The Rockies are likely demanding a hefty return for Goodman, and their asking price apparently was too steep for the Orioles to pay. Once again this appears to be an instance of the Orioles doing their due diligence on a player without ever coming close to actually landing him. Wake me up when something happens for real. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, major league owners met in New York, a week that sometimes sees interesting league news happen, whether that’s updates on rules, transactions, or other business. But this year, the meetings were dominated by the looming specter of the inevitable lockout, which is set to begin when the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) expires in early December. Labor Negotiations The news is bad on this front. Commissioner Rob Manfred gave a disheartening press conference on Wednesday in which he said, in so many words, that the owners would not ratify a deal without a salary cap. The Players Association, of course, will insist they will not agree — will not even negotiate — if a cap is on the table. Manfred went as far as to hint that they might bring the union in front of the National Labor Relations Board for “refusing to bargain,” and suggested that the political appointees in charge of the NLRB would be friendly to ownership, which is probably true. I’m not a fortune teller, but it looks like the owners are more committed to instituting a salary cap than they have ever been, and the players look to be fully aligned against it, and it seems like a near impossibility that the baseball season will start on time. Threats of legal action before the lockout even begins do not seem like a healthy place to start. Major League Baseball hasn’t lost games because of a labor dispute in over 30 years, since the strike that cancelled the 1994 World Series, but it certainly looks like we’re headed in that direction. Dumb. Manfred also suggested that he’s anti-Thanksgiving in the press conference. Dude is a PR nightmare. item.title: When will England play Norway and who could they play in Nations League semi-finals?
item.description: England will play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March, in a rematch of this summer’s World Cup quarter-final. Jude Bellingham scored twice in Miami as England came from behind to end Norway’s sensational World Cup run back in July. England’s World Cup came to an end following defeat to Argentina in the semi-finals but Thomas Tuchel ’s side are now looking to build on their impressive victory over world champions Spain in Madrid, which saw them top Group A3, by winning the Nations League for the first time. But Erling Haaland ’s team will be out for revenge after their incredible comeback to beat Denmark secured progress to the two-legged Nations League quarter-finals. Norway needed to beat Denmark in Copenhagen to finish as runners-up in Group A4, but found themselves two goals down inside 15 minutes. They fought back, however, with Haaland’s last-minute penalty sending them through to the quarter-finals for the first time. A place in the Nations League Finals, which will be staged in June and at the end of the season, is up for grabs for the winners. There have been reports of the Football Association expressing an interest in hosting the Nations League Finals, which feature the two semi-finals, a third-place match, and the final. Portugal, Italy, the Netherlands and Germany have previously hosted the Finals. When will the Nations League quarter-finals take place? England will travel to Oslo in the first leg before hosting the second leg as they bid to reach the Nations League Finals in June. The two-legged quarter-final will take place during the next international break in late March, with the dates of the two games to be confirmed in due course. First leg: 25-27 March Second leg: 28-30 March When are the Nations League Finals? The Nations League finals are held at the end of the club season and will be played at one venue in June. Portugal, Italy, the Netherlands and Germany have previously hosted the Finals, and there have been reports that England would be interested in staging them should Thomas Tuchel’s side reach the final four. The host country of the Finals is typically involved in the final four, although the Nations League could also allow the FA a test event before hosting Euro 2028 the following summer, with Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland also co-hosts. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
